entities.name: NAS COUNT
entities.description: A 24-bit counter used for NAS security, consisting of an 8-bit NAS sequence number and a 16-bit NAS overflow counter. Maintained separately for uplink and downlink messages per access type.

entities.name: NAS sequence number
entities.description: The 8 least significant bits of the NAS COUNT, exchanged in NAS signaling and incremented for each new or retransmitted SECURITY PROTECTED 5GS NAS MESSAGE.

entities.name: NAS overflow counter
entities.description: The 16 most significant bits of the NAS COUNT, incremented when the NAS sequence number wraps around to zero.

entities.name: SECURITY PROTECTED 5GS NAS MESSAGE
entities.description: A NAS message that is security protected, triggering NAS COUNT increment upon transmission or retransmission.

entities.name: UE
entities.description: User Equipment, maintains NAS COUNT counters for uplink and downlink messages.

entities.name: AMF
entities.description: Access and Mobility Management Function, maintains NAS COUNT counters for uplink and downlink messages.

entities.name: 5GMM-CONNECTED mode
entities.description: A 5G Mobility Management state during which inter-system changes and handovers occur, affecting NAS COUNT handling.

entities.name: Mapped 5G NAS security context
entities.description: A security context derived during inter-system change from S1 mode to N1 mode, with NAS COUNT counters set to zero.

entities.name: NAS ciphering algorithm
entities.description: Algorithm that uses NAS COUNT as a 32-bit input (24-bit NAS COUNT padded with 8 zeros in MSBs) for ciphering.

entities.name: NAS integrity algorithm
entities.description: Algorithm that uses NAS COUNT as a 32-bit input (24-bit NAS COUNT padded with 8 zeros in MSBs) for integrity protection.

relations.description: NAS COUNT includes the NAS sequence number as its 8 least significant bits.
NAS COUNT includes the NAS overflow counter as its 16 most significant bits.
Sending or retransmitting a SECURITY PROTECTED 5GS NAS MESSAGE increments the NAS COUNT by one.
NAS ciphering algorithm uses NAS COUNT as a 32-bit input (padded with 8 zeros in MSBs).
NAS integrity algorithm uses NAS COUNT as a 32-bit input (padded with 8 zeros in MSBs).
During inter-system change to N1 mode in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode, both UE and AMF set uplink and downlink NAS COUNT counters to zero for the mapped 5G NAS security context.
NAS COUNT handling during inter-system changes and handovers is performed in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode.
UE maintains NAS COUNT counters for uplink and downlink messages.
AMF maintains NAS COUNT counters for uplink and downlink messages.
